topic: Why did London's Millennium Bridge start swaying on its opening day?

(already covered, excluded); (9) Why do suspension bridge cables sing in high wind? (Engineering Marvels) 27; (10) Why do stadium roofs sometimes sway under a bouncing crowd? (Engineering Marvels) 26. Research (web search, each fact checked against two sources where possible): the Millennium Bridge opened to the public on 10 June 2000 and was closed just two days later after a pronounced sideways sway developed as crowds walked across it, VERIFIED (Wikipedia's 'Millennium Bridge, London' article, cross-checked against New Civil Engineer's 2021 report on the same event); on opening day, up to about two thousand people were on the bridge at once (out of a much larger total footfall that day, with sources giving figures from roughly 80,000 to 100,000 over the whole day), PARTIALLY VERIFIED (exact day-total figures vary across sources, so the script uses only the better-agreed 'up to two thousand at once' figure); Arup's engineers attributed the sway to a feedback effect they called 'synchronous lateral excitation' - as the deck moved slightly sideways, each walker's own balance reflex nudged it a little further to stay steady, and that fed back into more sway as more people crossed, PARTIALLY VERIFIED (this is the classic, most widely reported explanation from Arup's own engineers; a 2021 study by Georgia State University and the University of Bristol has since argued the mechanism is more about individual balance correction than everyone consciously synchronising their footsteps, which is why the script explicitly says nobody tried to sync up on purpose, rather than claiming people deliberately matched steps); the bridge reopened in 2002 after engineers added dampers to absorb the motion, at a cost reported around five million pounds, VERIFIED (Wikipedia and ingenia.org.uk's Arup retrospective both confirm the retrofit and the roughly two-year closure; the exact damper count is left out since sources disagree, 37 versus 91 across different reports). Myth: the assumption that thousands of strangers consciously marched in step together - the real finding is that nobody was trying to synchronise at all; each person's own instinct to stay balanced was enough. Titles (/50): 'Why Did London's Millennium Bridge Start Swaying on Its Opening Day?' 40 (chosen); 'The Bridge That Swayed Itself Shut in Two Days' 38; 'A Brand-New Bridge Had to Close After Two Days. Here's Why.' 37; 'The Physics Behind London's Wobbly Bridge' 35; 'Why Thousands of Footsteps Nearly Broke a New Bridge' 36; 'London's Bridge That Swayed Itself Off Balance' 34; 'The Hidden Feedback Loop That Shut Down a Bridge' 37; 'Why a Crowd Made a Bridge Sway Out of Control' 35; 'The Bridge Problem Nobody Saw Coming' 33; 'How a Crowd Nearly Broke a Brand-New Bridge' 34. Thumbnails: A a crowded bridge deck with a motion-blur sway effect (chosen, headline 'IT HAD TO CLOSE'); B a side view of a bridge with wavy distortion lines; C a single walker's feet with balance arrows. Hooks: 'On opening day in London, a brand-new bridge suddenly started swaying side to side - why?' (chosen); 'Thousands of footsteps, and a brand-new bridge had to close within two days.'; 'Nobody tried to synchronise their steps - and that's exactly why it swayed.'; 'A bridge this famous once swayed itself shut.'; 'Engineers didn't see this coming until thousands of people showed up.'. english.title: Why Did London's Millennium Bridge Start Swaying on Its Opening Day?
english.description: On opening day in 2000, thousands of people walked onto London's brand-new Millennium Bridge - and it swayed so hard it had to close two days later. Each walker's own balance reflex fed the sway, with nobody trying to sync up on purpose. Up next: why a crowd starts clapping in rhythm all on its own. #millenniumbridge #engineering #london #physics

scenes.text: On opening day in London, a brand-new bridge suddenly started swaying side to side - why?
This was London's Millennium Bridge. On its opening day in 2000, it swayed so hard it had to close two days later.
So what made a brand-new bridge do this? Thousands of footsteps, and the bridge itself started to sway gently side to side.

graphic.headline: Quick Chat
items: Why did it sway like that?
Thousands of footsteps all at once.
That, and the bridge itself moving.

scenes.text: Up to two thousand people were on the bridge at once that day - and that sway only grew stronger as more people crossed.
As the deck moved, each walker's own balance reflex nudged it a little further, step after step, until the whole bridge was swaying hard.
So no, people didn't deliberately fall into step together - each person was just trying to stay balanced, and that's what fed the sway.
Engineers closed the bridge, added dampers to soak up the motion, and reopened it two years later. Ever felt a bridge move under your feet? Tell me below!

hindi.title: लंदन का मिलेनियम ब्रिज उद्घाटन के दिन ही क्यों झूलने लगा?
hindi.description: साल 2000 में उद्घाटन के दिन, हज़ारों लोग लंदन के नए मिलेनियम ब्रिज पर चढ़े - और यह इतना झूला कि दो दिन बाद ही बंद करना पड़ा। हर चलने वाले के संतुलन ने झूलने को बढ़ाया, बिना किसी के जानबूझकर कदम मिलाए। आगे: भीड़ खुद अपने आप तालियों की लय में कैसे आ जाती है। #मिलेनियमब्रिज #इंजीनियरिंग #लंदन #भारत
hindi.hook_text: एक पुल जो खुद झूल गया
hindi.next_video: भीड़ खुद अपने आप तालियों की लय में कैसे आ जाती है?
hindi.pinned_comment: क्या आपने कभी किसी पुल या फर्श को भीड़ के नीचे हिलते हुए महसूस किया है? कैसा लगा?

scenes.text: लंदन में उद्घाटन के दिन, एक नया पुल अचानक एक तरफ़ झूलने लगा - क्यों?
यह लंदन का मिलेनियम ब्रिज था। साल 2000 में उद्घाटन के दिन यह झूला, और दो दिन बाद बंद करना पड़ा।
ऐसा क्यों हुआ? पुल पर हज़ारों कदम पड़ रहे थे, और पुल खुद धीरे-धीरे एक तरफ़ झूलने लगा।

graphic.headline: छोटी सी बात
items: और पुल के खुद हिलने से भी।

scenes.text: उस दिन करीब दो हज़ार लोग पुल पर थे - और जितने लोग बढ़े, झूलना उतना तेज़ होता गया।
जैसे-जैसे पुल हिलता, हर चलने वाले का संतुलन थोड़ा झुकाव बढ़ा देता, कदम दर कदम, और पूरा पुल ज़ोर से झूलने लगा।
तो नहीं, लोगों ने जानबूझकर कदम नहीं मिलाए - हर कोई अपना संतुलन बनाए रख रहा था, और उसी से झूलना बढ़ा।

graphic.headline: सब साथ चल रहे थे?
items: सच: हर कोई बस संतुलन बना रहा था

scenes.text: इंजीनियरों ने पुल बंद किया, डैम्पर लगाए, और दो साल बाद इसे फिर खोला। क्या आपने कभी किसी पुल को हिलते हुए महसूस किया है? नीचे बताइए!
